Definition: akin to G1032, G1031; to snort (as a spirited horse), i.e. (figuratively) to make a tumult:--rage.
BiblicalUsage: Phryasso means to rage, to snort like a spirited horse, to make a tumult, and it appears once, in the church's prayer after Peter and John are threatened. The believers quote the psalm, Why did the heathen rage, and the people imagine vain things, against the Lord and against His Christ.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the raging of the heathen is the world's oldest noise: kings and rulers gather against the Christ, and the church answers by praying the psalm back to God.
